title: SRS owner strategic map
purpose: The owner-governed release map above GitHub execution detail. It keeps semantic sovereignty and practical decision-making visible together.
bootstrapStatus: This JSON is a temporary curated source. Once the post-#256 model is usable, migrate its mission, boundaries, tasks and relations into an SRS repository and generate this map as a DocumentView or equivalent projection.

mission.decisionAuthority: The project owner is currently the sole decision-maker.
mission.purpose: Increase collective agency by helping groups develop the practice of making clear, accountable decisions together in an age of AI.
mission.muDemocracy: muDemocracy turns ordinary conversation into a living practice of collective decision-making. AI makes skilled facilitation and coaching more accessible; judgment, commitment and authority remain with people.
mission.srs: SRS is an open standard for portable semantic documents that people and AI can understand and use. Semantic sovereignty means a group can possess, inspect, understand, move, present and continue working with its meaning without dependence on the application, service, storage provider or AI model that created it.
mission.humanAiConstitution: AI may observe, extract, propose, question, organise, explain and coach. People decide, agree, ratify and remain accountable.
roadmapTests: Does it help a group practise and improve collective decision-making?
Does it complete the meeting-to-ratified-record loop?
Does it make meaning independently understandable and navigable?
Does it preserve meaning across tools, storage systems, AI providers and time?
Does it keep AI assistive and human authority explicit?
Does it establish or protect a root invariant that becomes expensive to change after release?

applicationStrategy.name: srs-web / app.mudemocracy.org
applicationStrategy.role: The first usable SRS application: an opinionated surface for people to inspect, edit, validate and work with their own semantic repositories.
applicationStrategy.architecture: One repository runtime and one canonical edit, save, import and export path. Repository, container workspace, facilitation and blueprint-authoring modes are projections over that shared substrate, never separate semantic stores.
boundaries: The application is generic about repository, Record, Relation, Container, Package, validation, navigation and preservation behaviour.
Blueprints select a workspace and presentation without changing canonical meaning.
Governance packages define decisions, roles, ratification, review and supersession; they are replaceable application content, not application-owned semantics.
Protocols guide work against canonical state; DocumentViews present it; neither becomes an authoritative store.
AI proposes visibly within a current Protocol or Blueprint context. Human review and ratification alone commit canonical meaning.
modes: Repository inspection and direct semantic editing
Container workspace for ordinary group work
applicationStrategy.predecessor: The separate decision-logger repository is a paused origin prototype and research corpus. It informs fixtures, scenarios and migration learning, but is not a canonical SRS producer, consumer or release dependency unless explicitly restarted on current SRS contracts.

tracks.name: Sovereignty

tracks.name: Decision practice

boundaries.name: Coherent Semantic Kernel
boundaries.actor: Maintainer of a first-party SRS package
boundaries.promise: One authoritative semantic model migrates and regenerates without silent meaning loss.
boundaries.durableArtifact: Migrated first-party corpus with generated conformance evidence.
boundaries.walkthrough: Regenerate the first-party corpus from the authoritative model, validate it through independent Node and Rust paths, and inspect canonical state through more than one DocumentView.
boundaries.compatibilityPromise: The migrated kernel has one source of truth and reproducible projections.
boundaries.stableAfter: Core identity, reference resolution and regeneration invariants are stable enough to build outward.

boundaries.name: Meaning You Can Take / SRS 2.0
boundaries.actor: Independent user with no originating-service access
boundaries.promise: A realistic SRS governance repository opens, validates, explains itself and renders offline as a self-contained semantic repository.
boundaries.durableArtifact: Portable `.srs` export, generic readable fallback and independent conformance proof.
entryCriteria: Archive, completeness and version-closure tests are defined
boundaries.walkthrough: Export an SRS-native governance repository or fixed governance fixture, disconnect from its originating service, then recover definitions, records, relations, provenance and a readable facet while accurately reporting missing evidence or unsupported semantics.
boundaries.compatibilityPromise: Frozen publications resolve their declared closure reproducibly and remain independent of live Views.
boundaries.stableAfter: The public SRS boundary: Continuity becomes the default.

gaps.title: SRS-web F2 portable-reader walkthrough
gaps.trigger: Create and make a gate when the SRS-web repository runtime can open a portable archive without service access.

boundaries.name: Meaning You Can Continue Elsewhere
boundaries.actor: Collaborator continuing work from a clone or export
boundaries.promise: A user edits offline, inspects semantic differences and reintegrates without losing identity, relations, provenance or unsupported content.
boundaries.durableArtifact: Reintegrated repository with reviewable semantic diff and preserved unsupported-content diagnostics.
entryCriteria: Diff and reintegration contracts are accepted
boundaries.walkthrough: Clone or export a repository, make an offline change, inspect the semantic diff, and reintegrate while verifying record identities, relations, provenance and opaque extensions.
boundaries.compatibilityPromise: Interchange never silently discards data a conforming reader cannot interpret.
boundaries.stableAfter: Offline continuation and reintegration form a reliable cross-installation collaboration boundary.

boundaries.name: Living Decisions
boundaries.actor: Group returning to its decisions over time
boundaries.promise: A group uses the SRS-web governance workspace to review commitments when due and supersede decisions with an accountable history.
boundaries.durableArtifact: Upgradable decision repository with living-decision history.
boundaries.walkthrough: In srs-web, upgrade a repository, identify a decision due for review, supersede it, and inspect the resulting history.
boundaries.compatibilityPromise: Package upgrades and supersession preserve prior decision meaning and lineage.
boundaries.stableAfter: The SRS-web governance workspace supports decisions as a maintained practice, not a one-time log.

boundaries.name: Facilitated Decisions
boundaries.actor: Group using the shared-screen facilitation mode of the SRS-web governance workspace
boundaries.promise: A group works through a projected semantic Protocol, agrees wording live and ratifies a complete decision.
boundaries.durableArtifact: Ratified decision produced by a resumable Protocol run and readable as a whole.
entryCriteria: SRS-web can open and edit the governance container workspace
boundaries.walkthrough: In the same SRS-web repository workspace, project a Protocol, guide the group through each stage, resume after interruption, review the assembled record, ratify it and later read it back.
boundaries.compatibilityPromise: The Protocol presents and guides canonical meaning; it does not own or alter it.
boundaries.stableAfter: Shared-screen manual facilitation is a first-class SRS-web mode, not a separate editor.

gaps.title: P2/P3 substrate split in existing story bodies
gaps.trigger: Before P2 implementation, move TSS emission and transcript-linked provenance from the manual P2 contract into P3 while retaining Protocol-run attention state in P2.

boundaries.name: AI-Assisted Decisions
boundaries.actor: Group using AI inside the current SRS-web Protocol workspace
boundaries.promise: AI reads a live or recorded transcript, proposes stage-appropriate text with provenance, and people edit, agree and ratify it.
boundaries.durableArtifact: Human-ratified decision with transcript-linked AI proposal provenance.
entryCriteria: Addressability and Protocol runs are available
exclusions: A separate AI-specific editor or canonical store
boundaries.walkthrough: In the same SRS-web Protocol workspace, use a live transcript, request a stage recommendation, edit it with the group, ratify the resulting decision and inspect the source provenance.
boundaries.compatibilityPromise: AI assistance never silently commits canonical meaning; attribution and human ratification remain inspectable.
boundaries.stableAfter: AI may participate as a transparent coach inside a human-owned decision practice.
